name: Nova Six
explanation: A six-voice programmable polyphonic analog synthesizer modelled control-for-control on the Roland Juno-106 (Owner's Manual, read cover to cover). One digitally-controlled oscillator per voice producing sawtooth and a variable-width pulse SIMULTANEOUSLY (independent on/off switches, polyBLEP band-limited), plus a square sub-oscillator one octave down and white noise, all mixed per voice; 16'/8'/4' RANGE selector. PWM with the MANUAL/LFO mode switch (manual = the PW knob sets width, LFO = the LFO modulates it and the knob sets depth). A 4-position non-resonant High-Pass Filter (0 boosts the lows, 1 is flat, 2/3 progressively cut the lows). A resonant 4-pole low-pass VCF that self-oscillates at maximum resonance, with cutoff, an ENV amount knob and its +/- polarity switch, an LFO amount knob and a 0-100% key-follow knob. A VCA with the ENV/GATE control-signal switch and a level knob. A single ADSR envelope (Attack 1.5 ms-3 s, Decay/Release 1.5 ms-12 s, Sustain 0-100%) shared by the VCF and, in ENV mode, the VCA. A triangle LFO (0.1-30 Hz) with a DELAY that fades it in, feeding DCO pitch (vibrato), pulse width and the VCF. The famous Juno stereo bucket-brigade CHORUS with all three positions (I, II and both I+II). Full performance section: portamento with its time knob and on/off switch, the bend lever with independent DCO and VCF bend-sensitivity knobs (DCO up to +/-1 octave) and forward-push LFO vibrato with its own depth knob, POLY 1 / POLY 2 / SOLO (unison) assign modes and +/-1 octave key transpose. Switch groups are bit-packed into single host parameters; the panel decodes and shows every individual switch.
